replies.text:
Prompt in Claude Tag

"Recreate Market Street, San Francisco as it stood on April 17, 1906, the afternoon before the earthquake, in Blender.

Scope: the Ferry Building up Market to Fifth Street, including the Palace Hotel, the Call Building, the Chronicle Building, Lotta's Fountain and the Emporium.

Before modeling anything, build a source file from: the 1899-1905 Sanborn fire insurance maps (footprints, heights, materials, occupants), the Miles Brothers film "A Trip Down Market Street" (April 1906), period photographs from OpenSFHistory, the Library of Congress and the David Rumsey collection, and USGS topography. Record every building with footprint, height, facade material, occupant, and the source for each fact with a confidence level.

Build everything in Blender Python. No downloaded meshes, textures or HDRIs. Write reusable generators (Victorian commercial facade, mansard roof, bay windows, awnings, painted signage, gas and electric street lamps, cable car, horse-drawn wagon, early automobile) and assemble the street from the source file, so every building traces back to data.

Provide a 10 second video up the street."

replies.text:
Perfect!

I have an idea for a cool interactive encyclopedia.

Image being able to wear a VR headset and you’re in like a museum walking around looking at art work and artifacts from around the world and from the beginning of time. 

This Museum has every display in it that all museums have around the world. 

Let’s say you wanted to learn about the ancient Aztecs, the AI takes all the historical written accounts from back then, all the pictures of ruins that remain, all the artists renderings of the location back in its day (if there are any), and all those deep ground penetrating radar sweeps of these locations, then it can reconstruct the entire location and populate it with the people and and all the time period accurate items.

You’d be able to walk around the Aztec empire and see jaguar warriors and rituals at the temples.

You could go to Ancient Rome, Ancient Greece, Ancient China, or anywhere.

You could even reconstruct battles in history.

Imagine sitting on the beach head watching D-Day, or decide to get a first person view from inside the landing crafts that day.

You could participate in the battles and get POV shots of warriors, or simply a bird eyes view.

We could even reconstruct personalities of people from history isle we have enough personal accounts from the person themselves or others at the time. 

Imagine going into a section of this VR museum and you go over to Julius Caesar, he then begins to talk to you, not pre scripted lines that repeat over and over, but real live conversations that are organic and fresh. 

You’d could ask him about how he beat the Gauls, he could then render a mini live realtime battlefield in front of you as he goes through what happened and how he responds.

You could click the battle and then all of sudden your at the tree line watching it happen, you could decide to get the POV of Julius Caesar during the whole battle. 

Imagine being able to witness first hand all of the greatest events in human history.

Pompeii, Ancient Egypt, Battle of Waterloo, Hannibal, Spartacus, Hammurabi, Ming Dynasty, Terracotta Army, Titanic, WWII U-Boat, The Bismarck, Ellis Island, Al Capone, Bonnie & Clyde, Gold Rush, Apollo 11, anything you can think of. 

That’s what I want to build for fun.
